title: Duplicate-sale prevention trace event state
description: Shape of the `state` field for duplicate-sale-prevention trace events.

guard.description: Which mechanism, if any, stops a repeated request from inserting a row.

dedupBy.description: What the dedup key is derived from: the sale's explicit identity or a hash of the payload.

day.description: Server clock, in days since the first request.

retentionDays.description: Dedup key retention window; 0 while no retention job has run.

request.description: The request being processed (absent before the first one).

inFlight.description: Requests being processed side by side; empty while requests are serialized.

phase.description: Where this request got to: in flight, check passed, inserted, duplicate, deduplicated, rejected, conflict.

dedupIndex.description: The server's dedup index, in insertion order.

dedupKey.description: The indexed value: the sale's key, or a hash of its payload.

sourceKey.description: The request key that first created this entry.

response.description: The stored response replayed for every later request with this dedup key.

sales.description: The sales table: one row per registered sale, duplicates included.

total.description: Sum of every row in the sales table — what the books say.

blocked.description: Repeated requests the guard recognised and applied nothing for.

duplicates.description: Sale rows written for a business action that was already registered.

lost.description: Real sales that can never be registered — dropped by the guard or swallowed by a stale dedup row.
